scores.evidence: Each phase relies on the one before it. For example, safe canary releases need observability
scores.rationale: Phases go substrate → CI → CD → observability → prod with an explicit dependency table and gating done-when criteria.
Phase 0 is discovery only; the first production path arrives in Phase 6, so there is no early walking skeleton.

scores.evidence: Make these decisions and write each one down as an architecture decision record (ADR)
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed in ADRs with some recommended defaults, but flip conditions or revisit triggers are not given.

scores.evidence: Include one with awkward dependencies so the hard cases show up early.
scores.rationale: Pilots run first and waves go simple to legacy, but widest-impact work is not explicitly ordered within phases, and the migration puts the easy services first.

scores.evidence: pipelines should get short-lived cloud credentials through OIDC instead of stored keys
scores.rationale: Security appears in Phases 1, 2 (SBOM, signing), 3 and 5, but is not stated in Phase 0 and the main checks come in Phase 5, so it isn't present in every phase.
Observability is deliberately deferred to Phase 4 and absent from Phases 0–3, which is the opposite of day-zero observability.

scores.evidence: Define the platform itself as code (Terraform or Pulumi).
scores.rationale: IaC, immutable tags, versioned templates, GitOps and build-once-promote give reproducibility across several phases, but not explicitly in every phase.

scores.evidence: Automatic rollback when the analysis fails. A rollback should mean reverting a Git commit
scores.rationale: Resilience is mostly in Phase 6 (rollback, game day), with little before it beyond runner isolation and pod disruption budgets.
The plan never states whether an AI layer applies, so it does not earn the N/A credit.

scores.evidence: Optional: preview environments for each pull request, for teams that need them.
scores.rationale: Some items are deferred (preview environments, portal in Phase 8, legacy last wave), but there is no explicit not-yet-built list with pull-forward conditions.

note: The plan has strong dependency ordering and a sound migration structure. It has no early production walking skeleton, it delays observability to Phase 4, it has no flip conditions on decisions, and it never addresses the AI layer.
